note:
Declared inputs to the dev / held-out split, committed deliberately.

`analysed_before_split` names every case whose criteria were read and discussed during quality work. Knowledge of those cases has already reached the people and agents who edit the skills, so they cannot serve as an independent check and are forced into dev.

`written_blind` names cases authored against a sanitised brief by an author with no access to any measurement result, and never inspected since. They are forced into held-out.

Publishing both lists is the point. This is a discipline split, not an information barrier: the suite is public, so anyone can read a held-out case. What the split commits to is not secrecy but restraint — not iterating against these cases — and an undisclosed split is indistinguishable from a convenient one.

2026-08-05, and this paragraph is the part that costs something. The `f03e327a57d2…` run measured the FULL suite, so every case then held out has had its result observed. Three of them were then iterated against directly: `cross-sensor-drought-comparability`, `mixed-datum-subsidence-refusal` and `season-confounded-fire-attribution` were read while narrowing the `change-detection` boundary, so they have been moved into `analysed_before_split` where they belong. The nine new v0.4 boundary probes were written by the same author who diagnosed the defect and made the fix, and are declared analysed for the same reason.

The 24 cases remaining in `written_blind` are a weaker instrument than the label suggests. They were blind when authored and were not consulted while making the v0.4 changes, but their results are known from the full run. They can therefore still detect a REGRESSION caused by the boundary narrowing, which is real and useful; they cannot confirm an IMPROVEMENT, because a case whose outcome you already know cannot surprise you. Any v0.4 report must state the held-out half that way and must not present it as independent confirmation that the fix worked. Independence returns only when cases are written by an author who has not seen these results.
